title: ShopEase Mobile Shopping App — Release 2 Product Requirements Document
summary: ShopEase Release 2 expands the existing M1 guest catalog and M2 NestJS catalog API integration into a client-ready Android demo with shopper depth: accounts, a merchandised home experience, search with sort and filters, guest and signed-in carts (merge on login), API-backed wishlist for signed-in users, full US-only checkout with flat shipping, estimated tax, single-use coupons, mock payment (no Stripe), order history and tracking with carrier details, in-app support, password-reset stub, and lightweight legal screens. All new delivery is planned under milestone M3 “Release 2 — shopper depth” with work items continuing from WI-010. Prices use integer minor units (cents) and ISO 4217 USD; order lines snapshot product name and unit price at purchase; order status follows pending_payment → paid → fulfilled → delivered (plus cancelled and refunded where applicable). Demo-safe operations only: mock PaymentIntent-style pay step marks orders paid on the server without real processor keys or webhooks.

personas.name: First-time Guest Shopper
personas.description: An Android user who discovers ShopEase without an account, browses the catalog, may add items to a device-local cart and wishlist, and can complete a purchase path that does not require registration unless they choose to sign up for persistence.
goals: Explore products from home, categories, search, and filters without creating an account
Build a guest cart and proceed toward checkout with clear shipping and tax estimates
Optionally register later and not lose cart or wishlist items

personas.name: Returning Signed-in Customer
personas.description: A repeat shopper who registers or logs in to persist cart, wishlist, and order history across sessions and devices via the API.
goals: Log in securely and stay signed in with tokens stored safely on device
See merged cart contents after login when a guest cart existed
Track past orders and order status from order history

personas.name: Deal-seeking Shopper
personas.description: A price-conscious buyer who compares products by category, brand, price, and availability and applies a single coupon code at checkout.
goals: Sort and filter the catalog to find in-stock items in budget
Apply one valid promo code and see discounted totals before paying
Understand why a coupon was rejected (expired, below minimum, exclusions)

personas.name: Post-purchase Customer
personas.description: A buyer who needs visibility into order progress and a straightforward way to contact support after placing an order.
goals: View order history and status progression processing → shipped → delivered
See carrier name and tracking number when an order has shipped or delivered
Reach support via email or an in-app form with clear response-time expectations

user_stories.title: Register, log in, and log out
user_stories.i_want: to create an account, sign in, and sign out with secure session handling
user_stories.so_that: I can persist cart, wishlist, and orders across sessions while keeping my credentials protected

acceptance_criteria.given: I am on the registration screen and enter a unique valid email and a password of at least 8 characters containing at least one letter and one number
acceptance_criteria.when: I submit registration
acceptance_criteria.then: the server creates my account with the password stored using bcrypt or argon2 hashing (never plaintext), returns an auth token, and I can shop immediately without mandatory email verification

acceptance_criteria.given: I have a registered account
acceptance_criteria.when: I log in with correct email and password
acceptance_criteria.then: I receive a JWT (or equivalent) auth token, the app stores it in secure device storage (e.g. flutter_secure_storage), and subsequent API calls include the token until I log out

acceptance_criteria.given: I am signed in
acceptance_criteria.when: I tap log out
acceptance_criteria.then: the auth token is cleared from secure storage, I am returned to a guest-appropriate experience, and protected API calls no longer use the previous session

acceptance_criteria.given: I am on registration or account settings
acceptance_criteria.when: I open linked legal content
acceptance_criteria.then: I can navigate to in-app Privacy Policy and Terms of Sale placeholder screens reachable from registration and account flows

user_stories.title: Reset password via in-app mock flow
user_stories.as_a: signed-in or returning shopper who forgot my password
user_stories.i_want: to reset my password through an in-app flow backed by a mock API
user_stories.so_that: I can regain access in the demo without real email delivery

acceptance_criteria.given: I am on the forgot-password entry screen
acceptance_criteria.when: I submit a registered email address
acceptance_criteria.then: I see a confirmation message that reset instructions were sent (demo copy may note production would email a link) and I can proceed to enter a new password without actual email delivery

acceptance_criteria.given: I completed the email step for a registered account in the mock reset flow
acceptance_criteria.when: I enter a new password meeting the same rules as registration (minimum 8 characters, at least one letter and one number) and confirm it
acceptance_criteria.then: the mock API accepts the change and I can log in with the new password on the next login attempt

user_stories.title: Guest cart and merge on login
user_stories.i_want: to shop with a guest cart and have it merge into my account cart when I log in
user_stories.so_that: I do not lose items I already selected

acceptance_criteria.given: I am browsing as a guest and add products to the cart
acceptance_criteria.when: I view the cart
acceptance_criteria.then: I see line items with product name and unit price in integer USD minor units (cents) displayed correctly, quantities adjustable where in stock, and out-of-stock variants cannot be added or show a clear error

acceptance_criteria.given: I have items in a guest cart and I log into an account that also has cart items, including at least one SKU that exists in both carts
acceptance_criteria.when: login completes
acceptance_criteria.then: the guest cart merges into the account cart by combining quantities for matching product variants and keeping distinct line items for non-matching products, and the unified cart is persisted via the API for the signed-in user

acceptance_criteria.given: merging guest and account carts is not fully implementable in time
acceptance_criteria.when: I log in with a non-empty guest cart
acceptance_criteria.then: the account cart is replaced by the guest cart (documented fallback) rather than leaving two separate carts active

acceptance_criteria.given: I am signed in with items in my API-backed cart
acceptance_criteria.when: I close and reopen the app
acceptance_criteria.then: my cart contents are restored from the server for that user

user_stories.title: Merchandised home experience
user_stories.i_want: a home screen with banners, featured products, new arrivals, and category entry
user_stories.so_that: the app feels like a real storefront rather than only a flat product list

acceptance_criteria.given: I open the app home route
acceptance_criteria.when: the home screen loads
acceptance_criteria.then: I see promotional banners, a featured products section, a new arrivals section, and tappable category entry points aligned to seeded categories (Clothing, Electronics, Home & Kitchen, Beauty, Sports & Outdoors)

acceptance_criteria.given: I am on the home screen
acceptance_criteria.when: I tap a featured product, new arrival, or category entry
acceptance_criteria.then: I navigate to product detail or a filtered product list for that category without errors

user_stories.title: Search, sort, and filter catalog
user_stories.i_want: keyword search with sort and filters on price, category, brand, and availability
user_stories.so_that: I can find products quickly in a catalog of roughly 50–100 seeded SKUs

acceptance_criteria.given: the seeded catalog is loaded from the M2 API baseline
acceptance_criteria.when: I enter a keyword in search and submit
acceptance_criteria.then: I see products whose names or relevant fields match the query, each showing price from integer cents with USD currency code

acceptance_criteria.given: I am viewing search or category product results
acceptance_criteria.when: I choose sort by price (low to high or high to low) or sort by newest
acceptance_criteria.then: the list order updates accordingly and remains stable for the same sort selection

acceptance_criteria.given: I am viewing product results
acceptance_criteria.when: I apply filters for price range, category, brand (from roughly 8–12 seeded brands), and availability (in stock, low stock, out of stock)
acceptance_criteria.then: only products matching all selected filters are shown, and clearing filters restores the broader result set

acceptance_criteria.given: a product variant is out of stock per seed data
acceptance_criteria.when: I view it in list or detail from filtered results
acceptance_criteria.then: availability is clearly indicated and add-to-cart is blocked or warns appropriately

user_stories.title: Wishlist for guests and signed-in users
user_stories.i_want: to save and remove favorite products on a wishlist
user_stories.so_that: I can return to items I intend to buy later

acceptance_criteria.given: I am browsing as a guest
acceptance_criteria.when: I add or remove products on the wishlist
acceptance_criteria.then: changes persist locally on the device only and survive app restarts until I clear app data

acceptance_criteria.given: I am signed in
acceptance_criteria.when: I add or remove wishlist items
acceptance_criteria.then: changes are stored via the ShopEase API and appear after I log in on another session or device

acceptance_criteria.given: I have a non-empty local guest wishlist and I register or log in
acceptance_criteria.when: the app offers a one-time import of local favorites
acceptance_criteria.then: accepting import merges local items into my API wishlist without duplicating the same product variant

user_stories.title: Checkout with US shipping and estimated tax
user_stories.i_want: to enter contact and US shipping address, review my order, and see shipping and tax lines
user_stories.so_that: I understand total cost before placing an order

acceptance_criteria.given: I have a non-empty cart and proceed to checkout
acceptance_criteria.when: I enter contact and a valid US shipping address (United States contiguous states acceptable for demo)
acceptance_criteria.then: the order review shows line items with product name and unit price copied at checkout time (integer cents USD), subtotal, optional discount line if a coupon is applied, shipping, estimated tax, and order total in minor units only on the server

acceptance_criteria.given: my order subtotal is below the seeded free-shipping threshold (for example 7500 cents / $75.00)
acceptance_criteria.when: I view the review step
acceptance_criteria.then: a flat standard shipping rate (for example 599 cents / $5.99) is shown as a distinct line

acceptance_criteria.given: my order subtotal meets or exceeds the seeded free-shipping threshold
acceptance_criteria.when: I view the review step
acceptance_criteria.then: shipping is shown as free (zero shipping line or explicit $0.00 shipping)

acceptance_criteria.given: discounts have been applied to the subtotal where applicable
acceptance_criteria.when: I view the review step
acceptance_criteria.then: estimated sales tax is calculated as a simple fixed percentage of the taxable subtotal after discounts (for example 8%) with copy that final tax may vary, and no multi-jurisdiction tax engine is required

user_stories.title: Apply single coupon at checkout
user_stories.i_want: to apply one coupon code validated against seeded promotions
user_stories.so_that: I receive eligible discounts with clear errors when invalid

acceptance_criteria.given: I am on checkout review with a cart meeting a seeded promo’s rules
acceptance_criteria.when: I enter a valid percent-off or fixed-amount-off coupon code that is not expired and meets minimum order value without hitting category or product exclusions
acceptance_criteria.then: the discount is applied, only one coupon is active on the order (no stacking), and totals recalculate using integer minor units

acceptance_criteria.given: I have already applied a coupon to the order
acceptance_criteria.when: I attempt to apply a second coupon
acceptance_criteria.then: the app prevents stacking and shows a clear message that only one code per order is allowed

acceptance_criteria.given: I enter an invalid, expired, below-minimum, or exclusion-violating coupon
acceptance_criteria.when: I apply the code
acceptance_criteria.then: no discount is applied and I see a specific error message (invalid, expired, minimum not met, or excluded items) without placing the order

user_stories.title: Complete purchase with mock payment
user_stories.i_want: to pay using a demo pay-now action without real card processing
user_stories.so_that: I receive order confirmation suitable for pilots and demos

acceptance_criteria.given: I completed checkout review with valid address and cart stock available per variant
acceptance_criteria.when: I tap the demo pay-now control on the mock payment step (PaymentIntent stub UI acceptable)
acceptance_criteria.then: no Stripe keys are used, card data is not collected or sent to our server, and the server creates an order in pending_payment then marks it paid for demo purposes without webhooks or external processor calls

acceptance_criteria.given: checkout reserved stock per variant on the server
acceptance_criteria.when: mock payment succeeds
acceptance_criteria.then: the order status becomes paid, order lines retain snapshotted product name and unit price, and I see a confirmation screen with a human-readable order number

acceptance_criteria.given: mock payment fails or is cancelled in the demo flow
acceptance_criteria.when: I abandon or fail the pay step
acceptance_criteria.then: the order does not remain in a paid state and reserved stock is released according to server rules for failed or expired payment

user_stories.title: View order history
user_stories.i_want: to see a list of my past orders
user_stories.so_that: I can review what I bought and open details

acceptance_criteria.given: I am signed in and have at least one placed order
acceptance_criteria.when: I open order history
acceptance_criteria.then: I see orders sorted with most recent first, each showing order number, date, total in USD from minor units, and high-level status

acceptance_criteria.given: I am a guest who has not signed in
acceptance_criteria.when: I attempt to open order history
acceptance_criteria.then: I am prompted to sign in or register rather than seeing another user’s orders

acceptance_criteria.given: I tap an order in the list
acceptance_criteria.when: the order detail loads
acceptance_criteria.then: I see line items with snapshotted names and unit prices, shipping address summary, and current status

user_stories.title: Track order status and shipment
user_stories.i_want: to see order status progression and tracking when shipped
user_stories.so_that: I know when my purchase is on the way

acceptance_criteria.given: I open an order in processing (paid/fulfilled demo state mapped to processing label for shoppers)
acceptance_criteria.when: I view order detail
acceptance_criteria.then: I see the status progression processing → shipped → delivered with the current step highlighted and processing orders omit carrier tracking until shipped

acceptance_criteria.given: an order is in shipped or delivered status with seeded demo fulfillment data
acceptance_criteria.when: I view order detail
acceptance_criteria.then: I see carrier name and tracking number in addition to the status progression

acceptance_criteria.given: order statuses on the server follow pending_payment → paid → fulfilled → delivered plus cancelled and refunded
acceptance_criteria.when: the app displays shopper-facing labels
acceptance_criteria.then: paid/fulfilled map to processing, shipped maps to shipped, and delivered maps to delivered in a testable consistent way documented for QA

user_stories.title: Contact support and legal information
user_stories.i_want: an in-app support screen and access to policies
user_stories.so_that: I know how to get help and understand terms before buying

acceptance_criteria.given: I open the support screen from account or help entry
acceptance_criteria.when: the screen loads
acceptance_criteria.then: I see the primary support email (for example support@shopease-demo.com), a simple form to send or simulate a message, and copy stating we aim to respond within one to two business days, with no live chat or phone

acceptance_criteria.given: I submit the support form with required fields completed
acceptance_criteria.when: I tap send
acceptance_criteria.then: the app shows success or simulated-send confirmation without requiring a live mail integration in Release 2

acceptance_criteria.given: I am on checkout, registration, or settings
acceptance_criteria.when: I follow Privacy Policy or Terms of Sale links
acceptance_criteria.then: I open static in-app placeholder screens suitable for demo and early pilot

non_functional_requirements: Platform: Flutter 3.x Android-first; the app must run on the Android emulator and pass flutter analyze and flutter test for Release 2 changes.

Backend: Extend existing NestJS OpenAPI and Prisma PostgreSQL 16 baseline only as needed for auth, carts, wishlist, orders, coupons, and optional read-only admin endpoints; new endpoints must have Jest/Supertest coverage and keep the suite green.
API scope discipline: at most 24 counted API operations for Release 2 (excluding infrastructure /health and /api/docs-json); include /health in the deployed contract.

App screen discipline: at most 12 new or materially changed shopper-facing screens for Release 2 (home, search/results, wishlist, checkout steps, payment stub, confirmation, orders, order detail, support, auth flows, legal may share screens where reasonable).
Money: all prices, discounts, shipping, tax, and totals stored and transmitted as integer minor units with ISO 4217 currency code USD; never use floating-point money on the server.
Inventory: stock tracked per product variant; checkout reserves stock and failed or expired mock payment releases reservation.
Orders: order lines snapshot product name and unit price at purchase; later catalog changes must not alter historical orders.

Security: passwords hashed with bcrypt or argon2; JWT auth for signed-in API access; tokens stored in secure device storage; support account deletion with minimum personal data retained (expose via API/settings as feasible in M3).
Payments: mock/demo payment only—no Stripe test or live keys, no PaymentIntent creation against Stripe, no Stripe webhooks in Release 2.
Performance: home, product list, and search results should load within 3 seconds on emulator against local/staging API under normal demo seed size (~50–100 products).
Accessibility: touch targets and text scaling should not break primary flows (browse, cart, checkout, order history); semantic labels on key actions for screen readers where Flutter supports them.

Privacy: lightweight Privacy Policy and Terms screens linked from registration, checkout, and settings; optional non-blocking verify-email stub only if implemented—email verification not required to shop.
Quality gate: complete at least one QA round on milestone M3 before calling Release 2 done; document scope in docs/PRD backlog.
Notifications: production push notifications out of scope—if touched, log or mock only.
out_of_scope: Real Stripe PaymentIntents, Stripe SDK card collection, or Stripe webhooks (deferred until production payment readiness).
Full admin panel UI (AR-01–AR-09); optional minimal read-only admin API for orders/products/coupons only if time permits without jeopardizing shopper features.
Guest-accessible server-side order history without authentication.
Multi-coupon stacking or complex promotion stacking rules.
Shipping outside the United States, dynamic carrier rate shopping, or multi-jurisdiction tax engines.
Live chat, phone support, or real email delivery for password reset and support forms in Release 2.
Replacing or re-planning M1/M2 baseline catalog list, detail, and API client except small deltas required by Release 2 features.
iOS store release, production deployment hardening, and full legal/compliance review beyond placeholder policy screens.
assumptions: M1 guest catalog UI and M2 NestJS catalog OpenAPI + generated Dart client remain the foundation; Release 2 adds auth, merchandising, discovery, wishlist, checkout, orders, coupons, and support on top.

Seed catalog includes roughly 50–100 products across Clothing, Electronics, Home & Kitchen, Beauty, and Sports & Outdoors with 8–12 brands and availability states (in stock, low stock, out of stock) sufficient for filters and demos.
Milestone M3 is titled “Release 2 — shopper depth” and contains only new work items starting at WI-010 (not duplicated M1/M2 items).

Free shipping threshold and flat rate use seeded configuration (for example $75.00 threshold and $5.99 standard shipping) and estimated tax uses a fixed percentage (for example 8%) on subtotal after discounts.
Mock payment marks orders paid for demo; shopper-facing status labels align to backend states for QA traceability.
Signed-in users persist cart and wishlist via API; guests use local cart and local wishlist with merge/import behaviors defined in clarifications.
Coupon seed data includes expiry, minimum order value, percent and fixed discounts, and optional category/product exclusions; one code per order.
Docker/docker-compose staging and GitHub Actions patterns from the repo apply; Release 2 does not require new production payment processor accounts.
Brand/visual identity beyond ShopEase working title may evolve without blocking functional acceptance for M3.
Optional read-only admin API priority: orders list/detail first, then products, then coupons—JSON/OpenAPI only, no admin UI.
